critic.method: Gaps are things a professional Indian and global content writer is likely to be asked for in 2026 that no card covers (zero or passing keyword hits). Weak cards are cards whose own text is contradicted, under-sourced or untested. Doubts are limits on what the verification actually proves.

gaps.gap: Indian commerce surfaces with no platform card: Meesho, Myntra and Nykaa seller listings (named only inside genre:marketplace_listing and genre:product_description), quick-commerce listings (Blinkit, Zepto, Instamart), B2B listings (IndiaMART and ONDC: zero hits), Justdial (named in genre cards only), property portals (99acres, MagicBricks, Housing.com: zero hits) and OTA hotel listings beyond plat:airbnb_listing.
gaps.still_open: Myntra, Nykaa, Blinkit, Zepto and Swiggy Instamart publish no listing rules that can be read without a seller login (checked 2026-10-13: seller pages are login-only, registration pages or prerequisite lists), so they have no card; MagicBricks refused every fetch; Meesho and Housing.com publish no character cap; ONDC's public specs set no length limit on item names or descriptions; Justdial and OTA hotel listings were not harvested.

Fix the test, not the card: give the brief 600-900 words of transcript (or cut the target to 600-800 words), then one re-judge.

doubtful: Seven of the ten kinds were never sample-tested: 440 cards (technique 127, platform 103, compliance 79, editing 45, tone 35, trend 30, language 21) passed the contract checks and were written from cited sources, but no test piece depended on them and no judge scored whether following them works. Platform numbers were source-checked at harvest: 289 limit rows, 250 high, 24 medium and 15 low confidence.

79 passing cards (69 genre, 7 hook, 3 framework; 76 when this report was written) had a CARD FIX applied after their pass verdict (fix rounds from 2026-10-07) and still say 're-judge pending'. Their verdicts score the card as it was before the fix. Most fixes enriched the exemplar_brief only (about 51), which is low risk; about 9 changed lint rules and 5 changed structure, and those changes are unverified.

Each sample had one LLM judge, and agreement between judges was never measured. No human editor reviewed any sample, and no native Hindi speaker reviewed the Hindi and Hinglish pieces, which only an LLM judge read.
Exemplar briefs are India-first by contract, so the US, UK and global use of most genre cards was exercised less than the Indian use.

Volatile platform limits, each read only once (2026-10-04/05), to re-check first: Instagram hashtags (5, changed in Dec 2025), Instagram Reels length (20 minutes in the app versus 15 through the API), Instagram carousel (20 in the app; the API reference went from 10 to 20 between 2026-10-04 and 2026-10-20), YouTube Shorts (180 s), X long posts (25,000 versus 4,000), LinkedIn job description (10,000 versus 25,000), Amazon backend search terms (200 versus 249 bytes, forum only) and the Amazon title cap (200).

21 cards rest partly on second-hand reading: search-engine summaries, pages that refused a fetch or sat behind a CAPTCHA, Wayback copies, or harvest notes 'not re-fetched' (among them plat:x_long_post, plat:tiktok_video, plat:tiktok_profile, comp:rbi_fair_practices_recovery, comp:emblems_names_act_1950 and five tone cards). Their quotes may be paraphrase.

Dated compliance that is moving now: ASCI's AI-labelling guidelines (signed 17 Sep 2026, effective about three months after publication), the IT Rules SGI Second Amendment (a March 2026 draft, status unconfirmed), DPDP Rules phases (consent managers about Nov 2026, main duties about May 2027, from a law-firm summary), EU AI Act Art. 50 after the Digital Omnibus proposal, Online Gaming Act 2025 commencement (secondary source) and the Income-tax Act 2025 renumbering of 80G.

Trends close to their half-life: trend:chatgpt_ads (12 months; U.S. test evidence from Jan-Feb 2026, India launch reported 27 Aug 2026) and trend:llm_readable_content_myths (12 months) need a re-check by early 2027; trend:hashtags_to_keywords' older evidence (2025-07-10) is already more than 12 months old.
Genre value tiers rest on marketplace category counts and salary-site figures read on one day (Fiverr, Upwork, AmbitionBox, BLS). They rank demand roughly; they are not market sizing.
About 20 language cards mark some rules 'house practice, unsourced'. That is honest, but those rules are a writer's convention, not sourced fact.

Wave C (2026-10-13) items that are moving or rest on a weaker reading: the E-Commerce Amendment Rules 2026 (start 1 Jan 2027, from secondary reports), Ayush rule 170 (omitted, but the Supreme Court left a fresh challenge open), EU Directive 2024/825 (applies from 27 Sep 2026, not yet in the consolidated UCPD read), IT Rules Part III (rule 9(1) and 9(3) under a 2021 interim stay), the SEBI (Mutual Funds) Regulations 2026 (new numbering from 1 Apr 2026); conflicting official limits kept side by side: Web Stories text per page (180 in the content policy, 280 in best practices), IndiaMART titles (ideally 5 words in 2026 guidelines, under 70 characters in a 2025 help article); the 99acres description cap is printed as 5,000 words in a 2023 guide and may be characters in the live form.
tool_limits: pcw.py check counts visible characters (grapheme clusters, with or without the optional regex module) and counts the platform's way where the source says so: X posts with X's weights (a link 23, an emoji or CJK character 2), SMS in GSM-7 septets or UCS-2 units, Telegram bios in code points, Google and Microsoft Ads double-width characters as 2. It does not implement TikTok's UTF-16 count or X's weighting on X surfaces other than plat:x_post; the platform cards say how to check those by hand (updated 2026-10-20).
Limits in seconds, pixels, bytes per keyword box and button or link counts are not lintable; the platform cards say how to check them by hand.
A platform with several fields is enforced one field at a time (--field); multi-part deliverables (message sets, bios, hook lists) are linted part by part.
Readability grades and the AI-tell list are English-only; Hindi and Hinglish drafts need a read-aloud pass.
